To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the number of hospitalizations for asthma and COPD is increasing in the elderly population.
the incidence of COPD and asthma in the general population is increasing and that this is due to population ageing.

the prevalence of asthma and COPD in Finland has been decreasing in the past 20 years and that the prevalence of both diseases has been lower among women and among younger age groups than among men and older age groups.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the Finnish health care system, and with the effects of demographic change and health care policy on health care services.
the effects of population ageing on hospitalisation for asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
the effects of ageing on health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a strong association between asthma and COPD, and that the association is not fully explained by smoking.

the use of inhaled steroids in patients with COPD is not recommended because of the lack of evidence for their efficacy in this patient population, but that the use of long acting inhaled bronchodilators, especially tiotropium and salmeterol, is recommended.
the use of inhaled glucocorticoid therapy in asthma has been clearly shown to reduce asthma exacerbations and hospital admissions and to improve asthma symptoms, lung function, and quality of life.

the population of Oulu is aging and that the number of hospitalisations for chronic respiratory diseases will rise.
the prevalence of chronic diseases increases in older people and this increase will lead to a higher demand on health care services.
the prevalence of asthma is increasing in Finland.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the number of hospitalisations due to chronic illnesses will increase in the future, and that the increase will be most pronounced among older age groups.
the number of patients hospitalised for COPD and asthma will increase in Finland.
